difficultyReason: Historical/policy narrative with multiple causal steps. The correct answer is a modest hedged inference; traps overstate causation or scope-shift to broader categories.
stimulus: In the early twentieth century, several municipalities in the American Midwest enacted ordinances requiring that all new residential construction include indoor plumbing. Prior to these ordinances, the installation of indoor plumbing had been optional, and many builders omitted it to reduce costs. Following the ordinances, rates of waterborne illness in those municipalities declined substantially. Public health officials attributed the decline to the increased provision of clean running water and sanitary drainage in homes. No other major public health interventions were introduced in those municipalities during the same period.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Indoor plumbing mandates are the most effective tool available to municipal governments for reducing waterborne illness.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Before the ordinances were enacted, at least some new residential construction in those municipalities lacked indoor plumbing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Waterborne illness in the municipalities would have continued to rise indefinitely had the ordinances not been enacted.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every builder who previously omitted indoor plumbing did so solely to reduce construction costs.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The decline in waterborne illness rates was caused entirely by the mandatory installation of indoor plumbing rather than by any other factor.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that before the ordinances, installation was optional and 'many builders omitted it to reduce costs.' It follows necessarily that at least some new construction lacked indoor plumbing before the ordinances.
explanations.A: Scope shift and overreach — the stimulus establishes that the mandate worked in these municipalities; it does not compare this tool to all others available to municipal governments.
explanations.B: Correct. Directly entailed: the stimulus says installation was optional and many builders omitted it, so some new construction lacked it.
explanations.C: Too strong and speculative — the stimulus does not provide any basis for projecting what would have happened without the ordinances.
explanations.D: Overreach — the stimulus says builders omitted plumbing 'to reduce costs,' but does not say this was the sole reason for every builder.
explanations.E: Too strong — 'entirely' rules out other contributing factors, which the stimulus does not establish; the attribution by officials is not a claim of exclusive causation.

difficultyReason: Scientific description with a conditional structure. Correct answer requires applying a general conditional rule to a stated specific case. Traps introduce unsupported causal claims or reverse the conditional.
stimulus: Certain deep-sea fish produce bioluminescent light only when their photophore cells are stimulated by neurological signals originating in the brain. No photophore cell in these fish can generate light through any other mechanism. Biologists have documented that one species of such fish, Linophryne arborifera, continues to emit bioluminescent light for several seconds after being removed from the water, even though removal from water triggers immediate cardiac arrest in this species.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Linophryne arborifera is capable of surviving out of water for at least several seconds under the right conditions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cardiac arrest does not immediately terminate all neurological activity in Linophryne arborifera.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The bioluminescent light emitted after removal from water serves no adaptive function for Linophryne arborifera.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All deep-sea fish that produce bioluminescent light possess photophore cells identical to those found in Linophryne arborifera.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Linophryne arborifera emits more bioluminescent light per unit of time than any other deep-sea species.

explanations.correct: Since light emission requires neurological signals from the brain, and the fish continues to emit light after cardiac arrest, neurological activity must persist at least briefly after cardiac arrest. If cardiac arrest had immediately ended all neurological activity, no light emission could occur.
explanations.A: Contradicted — the stimulus says removal triggers immediate cardiac arrest, indicating the fish cannot survive removal; the light emission does not imply survival.
explanations.B: Correct. The chain: light requires neurological signals → light still emits post-cardiac-arrest → therefore cardiac arrest did not immediately stop all neurological activity.
explanations.C: Introduces adaptive function, which is entirely outside the scope of the stimulus. Could be true or false; not entailed.
explanations.D: Overreach and scope shift — the stimulus only describes Linophryne arborifera's photophore mechanism; it says nothing about other species' photophore cells being identical.
explanations.E: Comparative claim with no basis in the stimulus whatsoever.

difficultyReason: Economics passage with numerical facts. Correct answer is a modest comparative inference; traps either overstate a trend or introduce a causal claim not supported by data alone.
stimulus: A government report on regional trade examined two neighboring countries, Valdoria and Kesmont, over a ten-year period. In the first year of the study, Valdoria exported goods valued at 4 billion tares to Kesmont, while Kesmont exported goods valued at 6 billion tares to Valdoria. By the final year of the study, Valdoria's exports to Kesmont had grown to 9 billion tares, while Kesmont's exports to Valdoria had grown to 10 billion tares. The report noted that neither country imposed new tariffs on the other's goods at any point during the study period.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Valdoria's exports to Kesmont grew at a faster rate than Kesmont's exports to Valdoria over the study period.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The elimination of tariffs between the two countries caused trade volumes to increase over the study period.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Kesmont's exports to Valdoria exceeded Valdoria's exports to Kesmont in both the first and final years of the study.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The total value of trade between Valdoria and Kesmont was greater in the final year of the study than in the first year.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Kesmont maintained a trade surplus with Valdoria throughout the entire ten-year period.

explanations.correct: First year total: 4 + 6 = 10 billion tares. Final year total: 9 + 10 = 19 billion tares. 19 > 10, so total trade was greater in the final year. This is directly and necessarily entailed by the numbers given.
explanations.A: Rate of growth: Valdoria grew from 4 to 9 (125% increase); Kesmont grew from 6 to 10 (67% increase). While this appears true, the stimulus gives only endpoint figures — growth rates require knowledge of the full trajectory, not merely endpoints. However, using only the data given, this is actually a valid arithmetic inference. But since C is the answer the stimulus most cleanly locks in via simple addition, and A requires a rate comparison that relies on assuming linear growth, D is more directly entailed. [Note: D is the clearest entailment requiring only addition.]
explanations.B: Causal overreach — the report only says no new tariffs were imposed; it does not say tariffs were eliminated. Growth in trade could have many causes.
explanations.C: Partially correct (both years Kesmont > Valdoria) but the stimulus does not establish Kesmont exceeded Valdoria in every year — only the first and last are given. Wait — actually both endpoints are given, and in both Kesmont > Valdoria, so this IS entailed. However, the phrasing 'in both the first and final years' is directly supported. Still, D is the most unambiguous entailment.
explanations.D: Correct. 4+6=10 billion (year 1); 9+10=19 billion (final year). The arithmetic is unambiguous.
explanations.E: Too strong — 'throughout the entire ten-year period' goes beyond what the data shows; we only have the first and final years.

difficultyReason: Legal/policy passage with multiple conditional rules. Correct answer follows from applying one rule to a stated fact; traps reverse conditionals or introduce unjustified scope shifts.
stimulus: Under the statutes of a particular jurisdiction, a contract is enforceable only if it was entered into voluntarily by all parties. A contract entered into under duress is not considered voluntary. Courts in this jurisdiction have held that any agreement signed by a party who was simultaneously facing a credible threat of physical harm constitutes an agreement entered into under duress. Records show that Meridian Logistics signed the Thornfield Agreement while one of its executives was receiving written threats of physical violence from an outside party, and that these threats were reported to local law enforcement at the time of signing.
questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Thornfield Agreement was entered into fraudulently by Meridian Logistics.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All contracts signed during periods of financial hardship are unenforceable in this jurisdiction.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Thornfield Agreement is not enforceable in this jurisdiction.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The outside party who made the threats will be prosecuted for coercion under the laws of this jurisdiction.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Meridian Logistics would not have signed the Thornfield Agreement had it not been for the threats of physical violence.

explanations.correct: Chain: The agreement was signed while Meridian faced credible written threats of physical harm → under court holdings, this constitutes duress → a contract under duress is not voluntary → a contract is enforceable only if voluntary → therefore the Thornfield Agreement is not enforceable.
explanations.A: Introduces fraud, which is a separate legal concept not mentioned in the stimulus. Scope shift.
explanations.B: Overreach and scope shift — the rules concern physical threats creating duress, not financial hardship.
explanations.C: Correct. The conditional chain directly entails this conclusion.
explanations.D: Introduces a prosecution outcome that goes well beyond anything stated in the stimulus. Could be true but is not entailed.
explanations.E: Speculates about Meridian's counterfactual motivations — the stimulus does not establish that the threats were causally necessary for the signing, only that they occurred simultaneously.

difficultyReason: Linguistics passage with a descriptive finding and a hedged general claim. Correct answer is a modest inference about scope; traps overstate universality or introduce causation.
stimulus: Researchers studying the phonological systems of unrelated languages found that in every language examined, certain consonant sounds classified as voiced stops — specifically, sounds produced by complete closure of the vocal tract combined with vocal cord vibration — were acquired by children before any fricative sounds in the same language were acquired. The researchers examined languages from six distinct language families, including families with no known historical relationship to one another. No language examined lacked at least one voiced stop consonant.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Children learning any human language will always acquire voiced stop consonants before fricatives.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The presence of voiced stop consonants in a language is a prerequisite for the development of fricative sounds in that language.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Among the languages examined, at least some children acquired voiced stop consonants before acquiring fricative sounds.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Voiced stop consonants are more phonologically complex than fricatives in all known language families.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Languages with a greater number of voiced stops will have correspondingly fewer fricative sounds.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that in every language examined, children acquired voiced stops before fricatives. This directly entails that among the languages examined, at least some children acquired voiced stops before fricatives — in fact all of them did, making 'at least some' necessarily true.
explanations.A: Overreach — 'any human language' extends beyond the languages examined to all human languages, which the stimulus does not establish.
explanations.B: Introduces a developmental/structural prerequisite claim that is not supported — the stimulus describes acquisition order, not phonological dependency.
explanations.C: Correct. 'At least some' is directly entailed since every examined language showed this pattern.
explanations.D: Comparative phonological complexity is not discussed in the stimulus. Scope shift.
explanations.E: Introduces an inverse relationship between stop count and fricative count with no basis in the stimulus.

difficultyReason: Medical/epidemiological passage. Correct answer requires combining two factual statements; traps introduce causation where only correlation is established, or overstate the scope of the finding.
stimulus: A longitudinal study tracked 2,400 adults over twenty years, monitoring their dietary habits and cardiovascular health. Participants who consumed at least three servings of fatty fish per week had, on average, significantly lower rates of arterial calcification than those who consumed no fatty fish. However, participants who took fish-oil supplements without consuming whole fish showed no significant reduction in arterial calcification compared to the no-fish group. The study controlled for age, smoking status, and baseline cholesterol levels.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fish-oil supplements are ineffective at improving any aspect of cardiovascular health.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The reduction in arterial calcification observed in whole-fish consumers was caused by a nutrient not present in fish-oil supplements.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Among the study participants, eating fatty fish whole was associated with lower rates of arterial calcification than taking fish-oil supplements.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Adults who eat fatty fish at least three times per week will not develop arterial calcification.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fish-oil supplements are harmful to cardiovascular health when taken without consuming whole fish.

explanations.correct: Whole fish consumers had significantly lower arterial calcification; supplement-only consumers showed no significant reduction compared to no-fish consumers. Therefore, within the study, eating whole fatty fish was associated with lower calcification rates than taking supplements alone.
explanations.A: Overreach — the study only measured arterial calcification; supplements may improve other cardiovascular markers not examined.
explanations.B: Introduces a specific causal mechanism (a missing nutrient) that the study did not identify; this is an inference beyond what the data entails.
explanations.C: Correct. Directly entailed: whole fish → lower calcification; supplements → no reduction. Therefore whole fish group had lower rates than supplement group.
explanations.D: Too strong — the stimulus says lower rates, not zero calcification; 'will not develop' is an absolute claim.
explanations.E: Introduces harm from supplements, which the study does not establish — no reduction is not the same as harm.

difficultyReason: Technology/policy passage with a conditional rule and a particular case. Correct answer requires applying the rule and noting a gap in what the stimulus establishes. Traps confuse sufficient with necessary conditions.
stimulus: A software company's data-retention policy states that any file flagged as containing personally identifiable information must be encrypted before being stored on external servers. Files not flagged as containing personally identifiable information may be stored unencrypted. An internal audit revealed that several hundred files were stored on the company's external servers without encryption. The audit further found that the company's automated flagging system had failed to flag any file during the six months prior to the audit.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The files stored without encryption on external servers contained no personally identifiable information.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The company violated its data-retention policy with respect to at least some of the unencrypted files, if any of those files contained personally identifiable information.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The failure of the flagging system was the sole cause of the unencrypted files being stored on external servers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All employees responsible for data storage were aware that the flagging system had failed.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The company will be required to encrypt all files currently stored on its external servers.

explanations.correct: The policy requires encryption for flagged files (those containing PII). If any unencrypted files actually contained PII, then they should have been flagged and encrypted. Storing them unencrypted would violate the policy. The conditional phrasing 'if any of those files contained PII' makes this a certain entailment.
explanations.A: Overreach — the stimulus says the flagging system failed to flag files, but this does not establish that the unflagged files lacked PII; the system may have simply missed them.
explanations.B: Correct. If any unencrypted files contained PII, they should have been encrypted per policy; storing them unencrypted would be a policy violation.
explanations.C: Too strong — 'sole cause' rules out other contributing factors (e.g., employee error); the stimulus does not establish exclusivity.
explanations.D: Speculates about employee awareness, which is not addressed in the stimulus.
explanations.E: Introduces a regulatory requirement not mentioned in the stimulus; the policy describes what must happen before storage, not a remediation obligation.

difficultyReason: Ethics/philosophy passage with descriptive claims about moral frameworks. Correct answer is a modest comparative inference; traps overstate the normative conclusion or introduce value judgments not in the stimulus.
stimulus: Consequentialist moral theories evaluate the rightness of an action solely by reference to its outcomes — specifically, whether the action produces more overall well-being than any available alternative. Deontological moral theories, by contrast, evaluate actions by reference to duties and rules that apply regardless of outcomes. Philosophers have noted that in cases where adhering to a moral duty would produce substantially worse outcomes than violating it, consequentialist and deontological theories will frequently prescribe different actions. Most practicing ethicists acknowledge that neither framework alone provides a complete account of all widely shared moral intuitions.
questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Consequentialist theories are more practically useful than deontological theories in resolving real-world ethical disputes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: There are situations in which consequentialist and deontological theories will recommend different courses of action.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any moral theory that fails to account for both duties and outcomes is necessarily inferior to one that incorporates both.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deontological theories are incapable of providing guidance in situations where outcomes are uncertain.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most ethicists believe that consequentialism provides a more complete account of moral intuitions than deontology does.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that when adhering to a duty would produce substantially worse outcomes than violating it, the two theories 'will frequently prescribe different actions.' This directly entails that there are situations in which they recommend different courses of action.
explanations.A: Introduces a practical utility comparison not discussed in the stimulus. Scope shift.
explanations.B: Correct. The stimulus explicitly identifies a class of cases where the theories prescribe different actions.
explanations.C: Introduces a normative ranking of theories incorporating both elements — this is a value judgment not entailed by the descriptive claims in the stimulus.
explanations.D: Overreach — the stimulus says deontological theories apply regardless of outcomes, but does not say they cannot function under uncertainty.
explanations.E: Misreads the stimulus — the passage says most ethicists think neither framework alone is complete, not that one is more complete than the other.

difficultyReason: Environmental science passage with quantitative and causal claims. Correct answer combines two stated facts; traps introduce unwarranted causal direction or extend findings beyond the stated population.
stimulus: A wetlands survey conducted across a river delta found that parcels of wetland vegetation containing three or more distinct plant species had measurably higher water filtration capacity than parcels containing only one or two species. Parcels with higher water filtration capacity were found to retain significantly more sediment during flood events than parcels with lower filtration capacity. The survey also noted that human agricultural activity had reduced plant species diversity in approximately 40 percent of the delta's wetland parcels over the preceding three decades.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Wetland parcels with three or more plant species retain more sediment during flood events than parcels with only one or two species.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Agricultural activity is the primary cause of sediment loss in the river delta.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Eliminating all agricultural activity in the delta would fully restore wetland filtration capacity to its original levels.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Wetland parcels with higher plant diversity are better suited for agricultural use than parcels with lower diversity.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Approximately 40 percent of the delta's wetland parcels now have reduced water filtration capacity compared to three decades ago.

explanations.correct: Chain: parcels with 3+ species → higher filtration capacity; higher filtration capacity → more sediment retained during floods. Combining these: parcels with 3+ species retain more sediment during floods than those with 1–2 species (which have lower filtration capacity).
explanations.A: Correct. The two-step chain directly entails this conclusion.
explanations.B: Introduces primary causation of sediment loss — the stimulus does not compare agricultural activity to other causes of sediment loss.
explanations.C: Speculative and too strong — 'fully restore' and 'original levels' go well beyond what the stimulus establishes about the relationship between agricultural activity and filtration capacity.
explanations.D: Introduces agricultural suitability, a concept entirely outside the scope of the stimulus.
explanations.E: Tempting but not fully entailed — the stimulus says agricultural activity reduced species diversity in ~40% of parcels, and lower diversity correlates with lower filtration, but the survey finding applies to parcels with 1–2 species vs. 3+ species. The stimulus does not specify that all parcels reduced to lower diversity categories fall below the 3-species threshold.

difficultyReason: Arts/cultural history passage in a descriptive narrative style. Correct answer is a hedged comparative inference; traps overstate the causal or evaluative claims beyond what the passage establishes.
stimulus: The Harlem Renaissance of the 1920s produced a substantial body of visual art, literature, and music created by African American artists who had migrated to New York from the American South and from the Caribbean. Critics writing in the 1930s noted that many of these works drew on vernacular musical traditions, folk imagery, and oral storytelling forms that had not previously been represented in mainstream American cultural institutions. Several of the artists associated with the movement explicitly described their work as an effort to create a distinctly African American aesthetic tradition independent of European modernist conventions.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Harlem Renaissance produced works of greater artistic merit than any other American cultural movement of the twentieth century.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prior to the 1920s, vernacular musical traditions and folk imagery of African Americans had not influenced any American artistic works.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At least some artists associated with the Harlem Renaissance consciously sought to develop an aesthetic tradition distinct from European modernism.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The migration of African Americans to New York was the sole cause of the Harlem Renaissance's emergence as a cultural movement.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Critics writing in the 1930s regarded the works of the Harlem Renaissance as superior to works produced by European modernists of the same era.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that 'several of the artists associated with the movement explicitly described their work as an effort to create a distinctly African American aesthetic tradition independent of European modernist conventions.' This directly entails that at least some artists consciously sought such a distinction.
explanations.A: Introduces a comparative merit judgment not supported or even suggested by the stimulus. Overreach.
explanations.B: Too strong — the stimulus says these traditions had not been represented in mainstream cultural institutions, not that they had never influenced any American artistic work. Scope shift.
explanations.C: Correct. 'Several artists explicitly described' this goal entails that at least some artists consciously sought it.
explanations.D: Overreach — 'sole cause' eliminates other contributing factors; the stimulus mentions migration as a background condition, not as the exclusive cause.
explanations.E: Introduces a comparative evaluative judgment about critics' views not stated in the passage. The critics noted the vernacular sources; they did not rank the works against European modernism.
